facts.fact: EcoMatin, on the BUNEC Director General's figures given on national television on 14 September 2026, says the pilot phase has digitised only 60 principal civil status centres of the country's 432 (a count it says includes diaspora centres and 149 special centres), a progress rate of 13.9%.

EcoMatin says 42 centres were already digitised in April 2022, the BUNEC Director General then citing eight municipalities of Yaounde and Douala and 28 other communes, with UNDP digitising eight Far North municipalities and German (GIZ) and Korean cooperation 20 other communes.

EcoMatin describes the operation launched in 2020 and steered by BUNEC as the digitisation of civil status acts, namely birth, death and marriage certificates, still far from complete in September 2026.
EcoMatin says the operation is stalling for lack of funds and that the progress rate has hardly moved since April 2022, when 42 centres were digitised, against 60 in September 2026.
The digitisation operation launched in 2020 is steered by BUNEC, the national civil status office, a public establishment.
BUNEC's Director General said on 14 September 2026 that BUNEC has a strategic plan and should reach completeness in 2029-2030 if it obtains the means it is asking for.

The project is now costed at FCFA 52 billion still to be mobilised, BUNEC having failed to raise the FCFA 27 billion estimated in 2018; its Director General said on 14 September 2026 that solutions are being found through cooperation and technical and financial partners; no budget line is given.
